subject: preview-analyze-admission-leftover.v1
role: The DR-131 leftover-design act for the seven classes D-148 recorded as having no live gate corpus — the analogue of provider-only-admission-leftover.v1 for DR-133.
verdictRule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Measured: 0 blockers, 0 SHOULD-FIX, 0 advisories.
acceptanceGrade: ACCEPT, unqualified. Application-grade for what this artifact is — a grouped measurement of seven leftover classes plus five candidate obligations — and expressly not a closure.

scopeOfThisAcceptance.whatIsAccepted: That DR-131 NT-1, NT-2, NT-3, NT-5, NT-6, NT-7 and NT-8 have no live gate corpus and no execution-obligation owner today; that they fall into five kinds; that the five proposed obligations, with their owners and claims, are the shape that would own them; and that all seven class texts are reproduced from the contract exactly.
scopeOfThisAcceptance.whatIsNotAccepted: This ACCEPT does not close DR-131's leftover-design, adds no DR-G* row, assigns no gate number, changes required-now from 19, and makes DR-131 neither eligible nor SATISFIED. The artifact says every one of those itself, and the token SATISFIED does not appear in it at all.
scopeOfThisAcceptance.whatItUnblocks: Later D-000 MF-6 acts that would add named DR-G* rows with these owners and corpora. The artifact is explicit that the rows must be named when added, which is the precondition I had to raise as an advisory against the DR-133 analogue.

obligationsAudit.form: Each obligation carries status candidate-not-adopted, notPerformedHere true, an owner, a claim, an owns list, and a numberNote refusing to assign a number.
obligationsAudit.numberDiscipline: Stronger than the DR-133 analogue, which proposed the identifier DR-G23. This one assigns nothing: purpose says it 'does not assign gate numbers', both G24 occurrences are refusals, and live file 08 has no DR-G24 and still holds 23 gate rows.
obligationsAudit.claimScoping: Each claim distinguishes itself from the live gates it might be confused with — the admission obligation from G23's provider FactCandidate and Coverage admission and from crash/malformed containment, the missing-rung obligation from G21's post-fault Coverage goldens and G23's domain mutation, the SARIF obligation from G17 with an explicit refusal to restore it, and the label obligation from G19's durable state-byte class. Those distinctions match the gate cells I read in the join cycles.
obligationsAudit.owners: DR-131's own owner column in file 08 reads 'Product + CLI / output', and three of the five proposed owners are that string or an extension of it; the SARIF one is 'Output/operability + CLI/product owners'. These are proposals for rows that do not exist, so no live cell can confirm them, but they are rooted in the row's own owner rather than invented.
obligationsAudit.conditionFourTrap: doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone says the classes remain leftover 'until later D-000 MF-6 acts add named DR-G* rows with these owners and corpora'. The word named carries the precondition I had to raise as CLAUDE-PONAL-V1-ADV1 against the DR-133 analogue — that a required row added without a recorded identifier would flip condition 4 from MET — so the trap is pre-empted here rather than repeated.

Each group is a distinct kind with its own claim, and the artifact neither numbers them, nor asserts they would all be required-now, nor performs any of them. Whether five rows or fewer is the right answer is the adopting act's question, and the artifact refuses to prejudge it.

consideredAndDeclined.item: The class entries carry no per-gate reasons, where the DR-133 analogue carried whyNotG21, whyNotG20 and whyNotG10 for each class
consideredAndDeclined.observation: A reader of this artifact alone sees existingGate none and a residual label without the reasoning.
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: The reasoning was established in join v2 and this artifact pins that predecessor at its digest with its role stated. Pinning the predecessor is how inheritance is properly evidenced in this corpus — the same disposition I reached for gate-harness-naming.v4's narrowed input list — and duplicating five gate analyses would add bulk without adding evidence.

consideredAndDeclined.item: The artifact does not say whether the five proposed rows would join required-now
consideredAndDeclined.observation: The DR-133 analogue offered a conditional cardinality statement.
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: That statement is what drew my advisory there, because it held only under an unstated precondition. Silence plus the requirement that later rows be named is the safer posture, and required-now scoping is properly the adopting act's decision.

independence.priorParticipation: I reviewed both joins this artifact descends from and the DR-133 analogue whose shape it follows, and my findings produced the NT-4 treatment it inherits. The risk is grading a familiar shape by recognition, so I compared all twenty-one class fields against the contract, set-compared the class list against join v2's leftover set, checked that the five obligations partition the seven classes, confirmed the gate table and the absence of DR-G24 in the live file, and tested specifically whether the condition-4 trap I raised against the DR-133 analogue recurs here. It does not.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no advisories. Thirteen attacks run, none landed. Read the scope before recording: this is a grouped measurement plus five candidate obligations, not a closure. DR-131's leftover-design stays open for all seven classes, no row is added, no gate number is assigned, required-now stays 19, and the row remains OPEN and not SATISFIED — the artifact says each of those itself, and the token SATISFIED does not appear in it at all. Custody is clean: 12225010 at 0444 unmoved, dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left fb6ba1f, file 08 at the 23cdf039 pin the artifact carries, COORD at e4ec0f6c, tree clean, and D-148 verified as adopted with a single heading. The substance holds under every test. All twenty-one class fields are byte-exact against preview-analyze-contract.v2. The seven classes are exactly join v2's leftover set, with NT-4 — the class discharged by named DR-133 execution — correctly absent, so the grouping conceals no measured ride. The five groups map one-to-one onto five obligations whose owns lists partition the seven classes with no overlap and no omission, and each claim distinguishes itself from the live gate it could be confused with, matching the gate cells I read in the join cycles. Number discipline is stronger than in the DR-133 analogue: nothing is numbered, both G24 mentions are refusals, and live file 08 still holds 23 rows with no DR-G24. The proposed owners are rooted in DR-131's own owner column rather than invented. And the condition-4 trap I had to raise as an advisory against the DR-133 analogue is pre-empted here: the artifact volunteers no cardinality figure and states that the leftover stands until later acts add named DR-G* rows, with named doing exactly the work my advisory asked for. Two items are recorded as considered and declined, both of which would have been new demands rather than findings.
